Hi Marta — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few ballpark numbers so you have something to share with the procurement/infra team before we sync next week.

Summary of discovery (from your answers):
- Expected steady-state: ~3M tokens / month (user-facing prompts + completions).
- Peak concurrency: ~60 QPS during morning batch windows (99th percentile spikes).
- Latency SLO: sub-250ms p95 for short-chat flows; heavier context generations can be 500–700ms p95.
- Data constraints: PHI-lite (hashed IDs only), strict EU data residency for a subset of records; SOC 2 required.
- Integration: will call models from your existing services in GCP us-central; desire for predictable cost and a path to private VPC later.

Deployment options (short form) and ballpark economics we discussed:
1) Hosted API (fastest path)
   - Pricing model: pay-as-you-go per 1K input+output tokens.
   - Example ballpark: $0.0045 per 1K tokens for the family of models we discussed (curated open model).
   - Pros: no infra ops, immediate compliance artifacts (SOC 2) + regional hosting.
   - Cons: higher unit cost at scale and limited ability to tune GPU instance type.

   Example math (3M tokens/mo): 3,000 * $0.0045 = $13.5K / month (variable).

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
   - Pricing model: monthly reserved GPU capacity + per-request compute surcharge (if bursts).
   - Example ballpark: 2 reserved nodes (A100-equivalent throughput) ~ $34K / month committed.
   - Pros: lower unit cost at scale, predictable monthly billing, isolation for SLAs.
   - Cons: minimum commit, lead time for provisioning (1–3 weeks typical).

   Break-even: beyond ~8–9M tokens / month cost favors reserved commit vs hosted per-token at these example rates.

3) Private VPC / On-prem
   - Pricing model: initial deployment fee + annual support/licensing + optional reserved hardware contract.
   - Example ballpark: one-time setup & validation $60K–$90K + support $8K+/month (plus hardware or customer-managed infra).
   - Pros: full control over data residency, on-prem compliance, KMS/HSM options.
   - Cons: upfront work, slower time-to-value.

Attachments: I've dropped a short workbook (BRW-pilot-scenarios.xlsx) with the scenarios above (hosted vs reserved vs private) and a brief pilot terms doc (redwood-pilot-terms.pdf).

Recommended next steps (pick one):
- Option A (fast): Start 30-day hosted pilot (we can enable EU-only region) + SOC 2 package; review cost after 30 days; schedule a short eval at day 21.
- Option B (predictable): 3-month reserved commit trial at the quoted capacity (2 nodes) with a $10K credit applied to the first month to offset provisioning overhead.
- Option C (privacy-first): Begin private VPC scoping; timeline 4–6 weeks to delivery if infra is ready.

Please let me know which you'd like to pursue and any procurement timelines (PO window, SOW/PO process). If helpful, we can do a 30-minute follow-up next Tue/Wed to finalize the pilot ask.

Hi Marta — quick follow to answer your technical questions and add an explicit reserve example.

- Reserved pricing above includes KV cache management and sustained throughput as part of the committed capacity. We size the pools with a 20–30% buffer above the expected sustained QPS to reduce cold-starts. Bursts beyond committed capacity fall back to hot-path bursting (short-term secondary nodes) with a small surcharge.
- Cold-start: for models with a 2–3B parameter footprint and typical KV cache behavior we see an initial cold-start penalty in the 250–500ms range for the first few tokens; sustained p95 after warm-up is typically under 250ms on committed infra.

Concrete reserved example for you to take to procurement: 
- Commit: 2x A100-equivalent nodes (multi-tenant reserved pool), throughput ~120 concurrent short-chat flows, sustained 50–60 QPS.
- Committed price: $34,000 / month.
- Bursting policy: auto-burst up to 4 nodes on demand at $8K / extra node / month equivalent pro-rated for usage.
- Break-even vs Hosted per-token at current estimate is ~8.5M tokens / month.

I added a quick table row to the workbook (BRW-pilot-scenarios.xlsx) with the numbers and added a separate tab with provisioning lead times and compliance checklist.

If you want a higher isolation profile we can size dedicated single-tenant nodes and provide an SLA uplift — we can add that line to the quote if needed.
